messages:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — after landing the int4 'v3-compact' build I ran our long-context sweep and saw reproducible divergence when the warmup prefix crosses ~48k tokens.
Samir Patel: ugh, can you paste the repro? is this prefill or in-flight KV mismatch? :eyes:
Maria Chen: Looks like a warmup handshake / phase resonance thing, not simple prefill. Repro command:```
python infra/kv_repro.py --model builds/v3-compact-int4 --prompt tests/long/48k_prompt.txt --dump-kv --seed 42
```
Maria Chen: Minimal log excerpt:```
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] STEP 1: prefill tokens=49200
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] KV_WRITE idx=49200 shard=2 offset=2048
[2026-03-18 14:02:12] INFER token=49201 -> token mismatch at layer 6
[2026-03-18 14:02:12] KV_READ idx=1 shard=2 offset=2048 (expected idx=49201)
```
Liam O'Neill: That read idx=1 looks like wraparound — but our wrap guard should kick in. Is this only on int4 quantized kernels?
Maria Chen: I re-ran on fp16 build and it's clean. So int4 path is implicated. Also happens when rotary_rope_scale > 1.0 in the runtime.
Anya K: Any difference with the new continuous-batching enabled?
Maria Chen: Test was with batching off (single request). I also tried with batch size 4 and the symptom amplified (more early wrap reads).
Jing Zhao: Could be an index truncation when compressing KV pointers into 32-bit for the compressed cache. Do we have a test that forces large absolute token indices?
dev-ci-bot: CI run started: eng-ml/kv-long-warmup/1891234567 -> status: queued
Samir Patel: Can you add a small instrumented run that prints raw KV pointers from the kernel? Even a single-layer dump would help. Also tag eng-runtime for kernel inspect. @eng-runtime
Maria Chen: Added a small diff:```diff
--- a/runtime/kv_cache.c
+++ b/runtime/kv_cache.c
@@
- uint32_t pack_idx(uint64_t idx) { return (uint32_t)(idx & 0xffffffff); }
+ uint64_t pack_idx(uint64_t idx) { return idx; /* TEMP: keep 64-bit for debug */ }
```
Maria Chen: When compiled this way the repro stops seeing wrap reads. So hypothesis: packing to 32-bit under int4 path + rope scaling pushes idx beyond 32-bit window.
Liam O'Neill: That would explain why fp16 is fine (different memory/codegen path). Also quantized kernel might use a packed struct for cache entries.
Anya K: We should add an automated boundary test: prefill at [2^32 - 1000, 2^32 + 1000] to ensure pack/unpack is lossless. Could be flaky on 32-bit indexes.
Samir Patel: Agreed. Also add a quick check in the onboarding checklist for new quant kernels: assert(kv_idx == unpack(pack(kv_idx))).
Maria Chen: Filing a short ticket: ENG-ML-7242 — "int4 kernel: KV index packing overflow under large RoPE-scaled warmup". I'll attach repro and logs.
Jing Zhao: For rollout, can we patch quick fix to keep 64-bit in pack for dedicated builds, and add a mitigation in routing to avoid huge absolute token offsets until fixed?
Liam O'Neill: Patch LGTM for emergency. But we need a proper root-cause: is the pack intentional for memory savings in quantized meta? If so, we need design doc.
Maria Chen: I'll draft a 1-pager and a unit test. For now marking the thread with :warning: and adding to tomorrow's standup.
Anya K: Thanks — leaving a note to check eval regressions (BLEU / perplexity) around the same window since subtle KV misreads can silently reduce quality.
Samir Patel: Good call. Ping me once CI reproduces.
Maria Chen: CI reproduced (see dev-ci-bot). Next steps: temp patch -> green CI -> ship to canary.
dev-ci-bot: CI run completed: eng-ml/kv-long-warmup/1891234567 -> status: failed (repro confirmed)
Maria Chen: Updated ticket with CI link and a tiny reproducer script. Thanks all.
